about.title: Coalinga Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Coalinga's economy leans on agriculture, oil field work, and the trucking that moves goods along Rt 33 and through corridors like Forest Avenue and E Polk Street — all lines of work where injuries happen more often than people expect. When you're hurt on the job here, California generally routes you through workers' compensation regardless of who was at fault, but that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or even another driver contributed to what happened, you may have grounds for a separate claim against that third party. Fresno County's mix of oilfield sites, packing facilities, and rural roadways means these overlapping situations come up regularly. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured workers in Coalinga with an independent attorney, free of charge, so you can get clear answers about your specific situation instead of guessing at deadlines and forms on your own.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Independent Attorney First

items.title: Clarifying Your 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires injured workers to notify their employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your workers' comp claim. An attorney can help make sure your report was handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Liability
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your only path against an employer, but a negligent equipment maker, subcontractor, or driver on a jobsite may still be separately liable. An attorney can evaluate whether a third-party claim applies to your Coalinga workplace incident.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job status, an attorney can explain your rights and how to document any concerning treatment.

items.question: Can I file a claim if my injury happened on Rt 33 or another road while working?
items.answer: Possibly. If you were injured in a vehicle-related incident while performing job duties near corridors like Rt 33, Forest Avenue, or E Polk Street, workers' comp typically applies, but a negligent third-party driver could also be liable separately. An independent attorney can review the details and explain which paths may be available to you.

items.question: What if my employer says I have no case because it was partly my fault?
items.answer: Fault generally doesn't determine whether you're eligible for workers' compensation in California — it's usually a no-fault system for on-the-job injuries. That said, if a third party contributed to the incident, fault may matter for that separate claim. An attorney can help clarify how fault does or doesn't affect your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim against a third party in Coalinga?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of the injury. This is separate from workers' comp reporting rules, so it's worth getting clarity early rather than assuming one process covers everything. Connecting with an attorney soon after your injury helps preserve your options.
